WebProxyTool captures and displays all network data that your device and installed apps transmit and receive.

How It Works:
The app creates a local on-device server and routes all outgoing HTTPS traffic through it. The app locally generates a trust certificate that should be installed and trusted to securely decrypt HTTPS traffic. When it is done, WebProxyTool captures HTTPS requests, makes dummy leaf certificates for requested domains, and acts as a man-in-the-middle proxy to read network data. Importantly, data is stored only in a local device database, ensuring user privacy, and WebProxyTool developers do not have access to it. The app works without any remote servers involved.

Privacy Statement:
1. The configuration profile and trust certificate are generated and used only locally on your device.
2. The app does not collect any data about the user, the user's device, or other apps used on that device, and thus the app does not sell, use, or disclose to third parties any data for any purpose.
3. The captured HTTPS traffic never leaves your device.

Working with sound, along with working with images, are two big topics in programming.

For me, as the author of this application, at one time it was a surprise that sounds in programming are associated with vibrations. Together they make up the so-called feedback effects.

The history of the creation of this application is as follows. In one of my applications, I wanted to use vibration. When I started googling and looking for information as usual, I found a list of all sounds along with vibrations at https://iphonedevwiki.net/index.php/AudioServices

And then I thought, why not make such an application where all the sounds and vibrations that are by default in the iPhone operating system would be presented.

No sooner said than done. I made such an application based on the table above. 

Also along the way, I added useful things in my opinion. For example, quite often when looking for a suitable feedback effect, one would like to know that the effect includes both sound and vibration at the same time, or there are only sound and only vibration effects. 

It was also found that a some number of sounds and vibrations are the same, and some are simply similar, i.e. the sound can be the same, but there is no vibration.

Finally, in addition to the Category property, I added my own classification of sounds into groups with similar mood and purpose.

In general, in my opinion, it turned out to be a very useful thing for finding a sound and / or vibration effect that can make your application more responsive and interesting.
